rows.text: returns -1 when `rcx` is null, when qword `[rcx + 0xB50]` is null, or when bit 0 of byte `[rcx + 0x318 + 0x160 * signed byte [rcx + 0xB48]]` is clear; otherwise it calls `0035BB00(signed byte +0xB48)` and returns the index of the first of the sign-extended dword `[list + 0x40]` 8-byte entries from `list + 0x50` whose first dword equals the result, or -1 when none does (or the count is not positive)

stages a stack block of dword 0, the zero-extended `edx` and the zero-extended dword `[[rcx] + 0xC]`, passes it with a 110-byte message callback to the 175-byte object allocator with size `0xC0`, hands the new object with `r8` to a 12-byte null-check-and-forward helper, and stores the object pointer to `[rcx + 0x18]`
builds a 32-byte stack block of qword 0, `rcx`, the zero-extended `edx` and qword 0 and passes its address as the only argument to a 292-byte routine, then returns through the stack-cookie check

compares the records that a 72-byte fetcher returns for `(1, word [rdx] << 16)` and `(1, word [rcx] << 16)`: returns dword `+0x58` of the `rdx` record minus that of the `rcx` record when the difference is nonzero, else the result of a 146-byte comparator called with the same `rcx` and `rdx`

fetches the record for `(1, word [rcx] << 16)` through a 72-byte fetcher; when its first dword is 6 it tail-jumps to a 146-byte comparator with the same `rcx` and `rdx`; otherwise it returns dword `+0x30` of the `rcx` record minus that of the `rdx` record, or, when that difference is zero, `word [rcx]` minus `word [rdx]`

compares the records that a 72-byte fetcher returns for `(1, word [rdx] << 16)` and `(1, word [rcx] << 16)`: returns dword `+0x5C` of the `rdx` record minus that of the `rcx` record when nonzero, else dword `+0x60` of the `rdx` record minus that of the `rcx` record when nonzero, else the result of a 146-byte comparator called with the same `rcx` and `rdx`

compares the records that a 72-byte fetcher returns for `(1, word [rdx] << 16)` and `(1, word [rcx] << 16)`: returns dword `+0x24` of the `rdx` record minus that of the `rcx` record when nonzero, else the result of the 130-byte comparator that orders by dword `+0x30` (with a record-kind 6 bypass), called with the same `rcx` and `rdx`

tries up to eight slots of `0xE8` bytes at `rcx`: each try resets dword `[rcx + 0x750]` to 0 when it is 8 or more unsigned, takes that slot, stores the index plus 1 back to `+0x750` and calls `00273A20(slot)`; returns the first slot for which the call returns 0, or null after eight nonzero results
